title: Football Basics
text:
Two teams of 11 players try to score more goals than the other team.

A match lasts 90 minutes: two halves of 45 minutes, plus extra minutes the referee adds for stoppages.

Only the goalkeeper can use their hands, and only inside their own penalty area. Everyone else plays with feet, legs, chest and head.

title: What Counts as a Goal
text:
A goal counts when the whole ball crosses the whole goal line, between the posts and under the crossbar.

It does not count if there was a foul or an offside before the goal, or if the ball was put in with a hand or arm.

title: Offside
text:
A player is offside if, when a teammate passes the ball, they are closer to the opponent's goal line than both the ball and the second-last defender (the goalkeeper usually counts as one).

You can't be offside in your own half, or directly from a goal kick, throw-in or corner kick.

Being in an offside position is only a foul if you get involved in the play.

title: Free Kick
text:
The referee gives a free kick when a player commits a foul, like pushing, tripping or holding.

Direct free kick: you can shoot straight at the goal.
Indirect free kick: the ball must touch another player before a goal can count.

Opponents must stay at least 9.15 metres (10 yards) away.

title: Penalty Kick
text:
A penalty is given when a defender commits a foul inside their own penalty area.

The ball is placed on the penalty spot, 11 metres from the goal. Only the kicker and the goalkeeper are involved, and the goalkeeper must keep at least one foot on the goal line until the ball is kicked.

title: Yellow Card
text:
A yellow card is a warning for a player who commits a serious foul, wastes time, protests, or plays in an unsporting way.

The player can keep playing. A second yellow card in the same match becomes a red card.

title: Red Card
text:
A red card means the player is sent off and must leave the pitch.

It is shown for very serious fouls, violent behaviour, stopping a clear goal chance by fouling or handling the ball, or after a second yellow card.

The team keeps playing with one player fewer and cannot replace the player who was sent off.

title: VAR
text:
VAR means Video Assistant Referee. A team of officials watches the game on video and helps the referee.

It can only be used for four things: goals, penalty decisions, direct red cards, and mistaken identity.

The referee on the pitch always makes the final decision.

title: Corner Kick
text:
When the defending team is the last to touch the ball before it crosses their own goal line (not into the goal), the attacking team gets a corner kick.

The ball is placed in the corner arc on that side. You can score directly from a corner.

title: Throw-in
text:
When the ball fully crosses the sideline, the team that did not touch it last gets a throw-in.

The thrower must keep both feet on the ground and throw the ball with both hands from behind and over their head.

You can't score directly from a throw-in.

title: Goal Kick
text:
When the attacking team is the last to touch the ball before it crosses the goal line (not into the goal), the defending team gets a goal kick.

The ball is kicked from inside the goal area, and it is in play as soon as it moves.

title: Handball
text:
It is a handball foul if a player deliberately touches the ball with their hand or arm, or if their arm makes their body unnaturally bigger and the ball hits it.

Scoring a goal with the hand or arm doesn't count, even by accident.

Inside the penalty area, a handball by a defender usually means a penalty.

title: Advantage
text:
If a foul happens but the fouled team is still in a good position, the referee can let play continue instead of stopping the game.

If the advantage doesn't work out within a few seconds, the referee can go back and give the foul.

title: Extra Time and Shootout
text:
In knockout games, if the score is level after 90 minutes, the match can go to extra time: two halves of 15 minutes.

If it is still level, there is a penalty shootout. Each team takes 5 penalties, and the team with more goals wins. If it is still tied, it continues one penalty each until one team scores and the other misses.

title: Substitutions
text:
A coach can replace a player on the pitch with a player from the bench.

Many competitions allow up to 5 substitutions per team, but the exact number depends on the competition rules.

A player who has been substituted off can't come back on, and the team must tell the referee before the change.
